terms.comment: Also spelled thūs, as in the Vulgate: the Magi offer aurum, thūs, et myrrham (Mt. 2.11).
The psalm verse is sung at Vespers in the East while the church is censed, and the old Roman Mass says it as the priest censes the altar.
Greek θυμίαμα; a fumigating compound in Celsus, the incense of the Tabernacle in the Vulgate.

phrases.latin: vīdēre quod postquam magī, Ēōa prōmunt mūnera, strātīque vōtīs offerunt tūs, myrrham et aurum rēgium
phrases.english: when the Magi saw it, they bring out their gifts from the East, and kneeling in prayer offer frankincense, myrrh and royal gold

phrases.latin: Dīrigātur ōrātiō mea sīcut incēnsum in cōnspectū tuō; ēlevātiō manuum meārum sacrificium vespertīnum.
phrases.english: Let my prayer rise like incense before you, the lifting up of my hands like the evening sacrifice.

sources: Lewis & Short: tus · Lewis & Short: incensum · Lewis & Short: thymiama
